findings.text: [Q01](#research-q01) 偏好终端内持续会话、工具/审批和恢复的开发者，需要确认输入属于哪个后端/会话及最终任务结果，原CLI/Web仍可做基线。
[Q02](#research-q02) 自有入口/Cordis挂channel与UI，输入经generation/FIFO到真实Host steer/followup、取消回执；[Q03](#research-q03) durable/transient译器和共享投影；[Q04](#research-q04)审批Promise/UI和救援启动门。
完整重核前稿六题/12findings；固定根DSH代表入口/Agent create-resume/真实输入/Host shell及取消、durable/transient译器与投影关键分支、同机claim、审批UI/回执、safe启动和root有界退出。未全审renderer/vendor、所有命令/删除/OAuth/更新/外部后端/插件生态和Host策略，规模非原创统计。
根终端客户端0.19.0/MIT、Node^22.19 或 >=24；Host primary0.2.2rc1及旧映射是源码合同/作者验证声明，本轮不等于发行安装通过。

| 阶段 | 现金与资源 | 人工与时间 |
|---|---|---|
| 首次 | 包/渲染依赖/缓存/后端资源未知 | 版本/profile/TTY/备份配置分钟未知 |
| 持续 | 后端模型/工具、终端CPU/缓存日志未知 | 快捷键/审批与状态维护，净节时未测 |
| 失败恢复 | 重连/重试/重复作业资源未知 | 核JSONL/稳定行/ledger/队列，分钟未知 |
| 退出 | 已发生工具/模型用量未知 | 草稿/后台/文件与共享home残留另核 |
[Q05](#research-q05) 独立home低敏会话先核输入所属/普通取消保队列，恢复按[Q03](#research-q03)比持久稳定行。审批背景与external先核不明则拒；中断未知先不重送，保存ID后退CLI/Web。safe仅排障组合，后端凭据与已发生副作用另核。

| 效果项 | 源码支持 | 尚不能证明 |
|---|---|---|
| 交互 | 真实Host输入/终端挂载 | 相比CLI/Web任务更快/可访问性好 |
| 恢复 | seq/callId/generation、共投影 | 所有迟到/重复最终一致 |
| 取消 | user保inbox、interrupt回执防重送 | 工具/外部进程停止和副作用撤销 |
| 审批 | key/来源badge/一次决定回接 | 来源认证/跨账户隔离 |
| 退出 | disposal/unload/有界fallback | 无残留或home还原 |
[Q02](#research-q02)输入generation/FIFO和取消receipt防双送，[Q03](#research-q03)seq/callId/严格ledger与[Q04](#research-q04)面板key/来源标记有局部价值；同步Host输入契约、历史fallback、后台ask和5秒退出各有边界，不由大仓/回归文件数推可靠性。

[Q02](#research-q02)真实输入捕获session/generation、拒绝/held dock和不同取消回执，[Q03](#research-q03)durable seq/callId投影及同机claim，[Q04](#research-q04)审批陈旧key/重复标记与safe门形成具体终端接线贡献。Host Agent/权限/存储、第三方后端和底层renderer依赖分开归因，不用仓库体量或品牌证明效果。
[Q02](#research-q02) accepted/confirmed只到输入与队列，工具副作用不回滚；[Q03](#research-q03)live/history有意不同、迟到fallback会跳过，[Q04](#research-q04)external badge非身份证明且safe仍共享home凭据。若用户把界面状态当执行/隔离完成，就可能误重送或错批。
[Q06](#research-q06)用同durable日志验证并诊断最终稳定行/队列一致，排除刻意live-only帧；对照现有debug+人工JSONL核重复/reset/迟到/切会话/未知取消回执，漏行/误归属/双送或诊断假相等即推翻。已有共享projector不当新发明，无运行原型。

| 依赖或条件 | 具体版本/作用 | 缺失或边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 客户端 | @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui0.19.0，MIT | bin与Cordis入口，非新Agent内核 |
| Node/终端 | ^22.19 或 >=24及合适TTY | 终端宽度/模式需实际验 |
| DSH | contract primary0.2.2-rc.1；旧family映射/peer更宽 | 本轮未验安装/CI，drift不等于兼容成功 |
| Host服务 | Agent/会话/模型/工具/审批/持久化与shell | 权限/副作用仍归实际后端 |
| 其他后端 | Claude SDK/Codex等各自运行/权限 | 本稿不外推DSH契约 |
| home/凭据 | 独立低权限试验根、备份 | safe profile仍同home，不隔离账户 |

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)至[Q04](#research-q04)：novelty9为成熟Host/React终端与后端中立会话/投影接缝的组合，超过无适配0；非新Agent执行协议到18。mechanism15的enqueue generation、receipt dock撤销、seq/callId和ledger严格拒绝对局部误归属/双送作具体取舍，超过薄封装8；相对原CLI/Web未解关键任务正确性/审批来源与恢复一致验证，不到23。transferability10的AgentSession/共享投影和稳定行诊断可迁其他终端后端，超过页面私有5；DSH legacy/多backend契约与renderer耦合，主要反例history迟到、后台ask/退出仍需复核，不到15。simplification8用同projector/输入及权限接口连接多个视图/后端，超过入口4；own renderer/vendor/profile/adapter和兼容线仍复杂，未证整体维护负担下降到11。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q05](#research-q05)：workflow0，终端内状态/审批仍同用户驱动Host与检查结果，没有已核组织分工/交接责任变化到9，不能按集中入口计。delivery0，仍交付原Host会话/代码与工具结果，终端投影不构成新验收对象到8。reach0，仍需Node/Host/终端配置技能，未识别此前受限明确人群到5，偏好终端不是新增可达性证据。economics0，用户仍提供模型/工具资源、凭据与恢复维护，未识别供给/计价/资源组织/服务风险结构变化到4；费用与人时未测另列，不能由cost estimate/少切窗口加经济创新。

recommendation.reason: 偏好终端会话、能核 Host 权限与持久日志的开发者，可固定 0.19.0 和实际后端，在独立 home 用低敏样例试输入、恢复和审批。它把流状态与后端操作接到一套终端投影和队列接口，终端偏好以外相对原 CLI/Web 的任务增益仍未证明，普通取消也会保留待发输入。出现误归属、漏行、来源不明或中断回执不确定就停止重送并回 CLI/Web 核日志和副作用，safe profile 不能代替 home 与凭据隔离。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)终端持续会话和[Q02](#research-q02)/[Q04](#research-q04)实际输入/审批有具体反复任务，超过一般用途15；缺用户频次和重要性对照不到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)原CLI/Web已有核心任务，终端交互/集中状态有偏好增量超过无用0；[Q02](#research-q02)/[Q03](#research-q03)接缝正确性是使新前端可用，尚未证明比直接替代多完成任务到13，不能因功能多加分。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)UI/input→submit→Host和取消失败、[Q03](#research-q03)真实译器/投影与claim、[Q04](#research-q04)审批回接/safe程序门均核到callee，超片段6；限定DSH代表链、未运行目标/终端/模型/效果，不能到19。

cost.rationale: [Q05](#research-q05)独立home、低敏会话与原CLI/Web退路可局部控，超无可行恢复0；[Q02](#research-q02)保队列/有界强退、[Q04](#research-q04)共享home/凭据和多兼容线使恢复/退出费用未知，未到10。

publication.summaries.text: 为 DeepSeek Harness 提供交互式终端客户端、实时状态、会话投影与审批界面。

items.界面: 终端会话、实时/历史投影、状态及前后台审批。
items.用户命令: 输入、steer/followup、取消/恢复与Host shell接缝。
items.后台: 自有组合入口、后端适配、同机挂载ledger和有界退出。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 终端会话 | 流、状态与键盘操作 | client，执行域属Host/后端 |
| 输入/取消 | FIFO提交、pending/dock与回执 | accepted非完成，user cancel保inbox |
| 历史投影 | durable seq/callId恢复与实时共用 | live-only表现不同，迟到fallback可跳过 |
| 审批 | 前台/后台ask、一次批准/拒绝 | external是提醒，非来源认证 |
| safe/退出 | 救援profile与root清理 | 共享home/凭据，5秒fallback非回滚 |

publication.advice.text: [Q05](#research-q05) 独立home低敏会话先核输入所属/普通取消保队列，恢复按[Q03](#research-q03)比持久稳定行。审批背景与external先核不明则拒；中断未知先不重送，保存ID后退CLI/Web。safe仅排障组合，后端凭据与已发生副作用另核。

      "content": "<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"docs/assets/readme/logo-en.svg\" alt=\"dsh-TUI animated whale logo\" width=\"560\">\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <strong>English</strong> | <a href=\"README_ZH.md\">简体中文</a>\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui\"><img alt=\"npm\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui?style=flat-square&color=4b6fff\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/actions/workflows/ci.yml\"><img alt=\"CI\" src=\"https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg\"></a>\n  <a href=\"LICENSE\"><img alt=\"MIT License\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-263146?style=flat-square\"></a>\n  <img alt=\"Public beta\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/status-public%20beta-7da1de?style=flat-square\">\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/stargazers\"><img alt=\"GitHub stars\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/github/stars/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI?style=flat-square&color=4b6fff\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui\"><img alt=\"npm downloads\" src=\"https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui?style=flat-square&color=4b6fff\"></a>\n</p>\n\n# dsh-TUI\n\n> An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale\n> header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a\n> context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only\n> DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its\n> own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party\n> backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind.\nThe prompt footer hides completed goals once the turn is idle; the Todo side panel retains their history. `Ctrl+Q` folds todos while working and hides/restores the idle goal/todo footer. Clicking its todo header also hides it while idle. Hiding changes only this display: a new goal/todo snapshot or session reveals it again, and `/goal clear` does not clear todos.\n\nSplit diff cards give one-sided additions and deletions the full body width, without an empty opposite pane. Ordinary edits remain side by side, and mixed files choose their layout separately before folding or streaming reveal.\n\nCompaction status stays on one line in narrow panes: phase and cancellation hints yield first, then the label is shortened; elapsed time is shown only as a complete field.\n\nImage files referenced with `@path` use the same admission and resize/conversion policy as pasted images. Adjustment notices report the stored dimensions and format; required animation conversion is refused instead of dropping frames. Mention images and staged images still share count and stored-byte limits in source order.\n\n\n## Highlights\n\nPanels without a verified Component identity are temporary: settings show their title and a distinct number for this run. Their toggles take effect immediately without being saved, and unrelated settings changes preserve that choice. Old `actN:panel` entries cannot be mapped safely: remove the placeholder and select the current panel again. Verified Components named `actN` keep their public runtime address; an explicit selection uses `component:actN:panel` in saved preferences to avoid claiming an old anonymous entry.\n\nThe default reasoning-effort setting offers the current backend/model’s declared tiers, including custom IDs. Saved values absent from that catalog stay visible and stored; while loading or unavailable, only Auto is selectable. On DSH, Auto follows the saved `/effort` choice, then the configured effort, then the model default. Claude/Codex retain backend preferences for Auto at startup and for resumed sessions; explicitly choosing Auto resets the model default. Explicit settings changes affect the next request; unsupported preferences fall back with a notice and are never forced onto a route.\n\nResuming a DSH session preserves its recorded reasoning effort (or its live selection when reattaching). The saved default seeds new sessions; explicit `/effort` and effort-default settings changes still apply to the current session’s next request.\n\n\n- **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task.\n- **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (accounts & models / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`; its first step signs in to a subscription and catches the models it brings in (none → no question, one → that one, several → you choose), or adds an API key through the `/provider` wizard, which asks which of the enabled models to switch to or keeps the current one.\n- **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI.\n- **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, `bel`, or `windows`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. On local Windows, `auto` resolves to `windows`, the system's native notifications: a task-completion toast. The first toast registers that user's AppUserModelID under HKCU, the toast appears about 3 seconds after the task ends (the PowerShell cold start that buys the no-extra-install route), and for DSH sessions an enabled, active external DSH notification plugin in the running profile makes dsh-TUI yield to it (no toast, no bell); an installed but disabled plugin does not suppress notifications; if that AppUserModelID cannot be written, the notification falls back to the bell instead of going silent. SSH sessions keep the attached terminal's notification protocol in `auto` mode; explicit `windows` still selects the host's native transport. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes.\n- **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal.\n- **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals.\n- **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams.\n- **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals.\n- **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter.\n- **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. All eight built-in panels are enabled by default, and so are plugin panels registered later (`sidePanel.panels: '*'`; untick a row in `/settings` to switch to an explicit list). The header shows each inactive panel's symbol; hover to see its name. Narrow terminals and inline mode keep full-screen panels. In the `todo` panel a long goal wraps to the panel width with its phase on a separate row; when the content exceeds the viewport, focus the panel and scroll with `↑`/`↓` or the wheel (every todo is reachable too) (the compact goal row above the chat input stays a single truncated line with a hover tooltip).\n- **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Title, trajectory-strip and session-state animations update independently of the transcript and pause when idle or unfocused.\n  Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details.\n- **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`.\n- **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor.\n  `/btw` uses an overlay when its sidebar cannot render. Main-task questionnaires and the fullscreen draft editor take priority while preserving the side question and draft.\n- **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt.\n- **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires.\n- **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin.\n  A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned.\n- **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more.\n- **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches.\n\nKeys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md).\n\nPlugin side panels stay enabled when unrelated settings change. Editing the enabled panel list still applies your explicit selection.\n\n\nWorkspace side-panel counts match the session manager: the current conversation counts; empty logs, subagents, fork ancestors and archived sessions do not. Registered workspaces with no visible conversations remain at zero. Loading and read errors are shown separately; press `r` to refresh.\n\nWhen a DSH 0.2.1+ Agent moves its session to another directory (the `working_directory` tool or a Git worktree), the status line, Git branch, `@` completion, `!` commands, clicked paths, skill commands and loaded context follow it, including after `/resume`. The session stays registered under the project it started in. Relative paths in cards rendered before a move resolve against the session's current directory when clicked; absolute paths keep their target.\n\nFullscreen mouse selection stays in the pane where the gesture starts, including chat, sidebar and either diff column. Diagonal, word and line selection copy that pane’s text; soft wraps join independently, source newlines remain, and divider drags only resize.\n\n## Preview\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n  <picture>\n    <source media=\"(max-width: 640px)\" srcset=\"docs/assets/readme/preview-en-mobile.svg\">\n    <img src=\"docs/assets/readme/preview-en.svg\" alt=\"Recorded dsh-TUI session: welcome, completion, help and typing, with animated pixel whale.\" width=\"78%\">\n  </picture>\n</div>\n\n## Featured & Listed\n\nAmong the community plugins recommended by the **official lead of DeepSeek\nHarness**, dsh-TUI is the first.\n\nFeatured by the **DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account**, listed in the\n[dshfind](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) plugin\ndirectory, and ranked **#7 on [GitHub Trending](https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168)\ndaily** (TypeScript).\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n  <table>\n    <tr>\n      <td align=\"center\" valign=\"middle\" width=\"50%\">\n        <img src=\"screenshots/wechat-official.png\" alt=\"dsh-TUI featured by the DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account\" width=\"480\">\n        <br>\n        <strong>Featured by the official WeChat account</strong>\n      </td>\n      <td align=\"center\" valign=\"middle\" width=\"50%\">\n        <a href=\"https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI\"><img src=\"https://dshfind.com/api/card/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI?lang=en\" alt=\"dsh-TUI on dshfind\" width=\"420\"></a>\n        <br>\n        <strong>Listed in the dshfind directory</strong>\n        <br><br>\n        <a href=\"https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168\" title=\"GitHub Trending Daily #7 · TypeScript\"><img alt=\"Trendshift\" src=\"https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/146168/daily?language=TypeScript\"></a>\n        <br>\n        <strong>GitHub Trending Daily #7</strong>\n      </td>\n    </tr>\n  </table>\n</div>\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Windows one-click installer (x64)\n\nDownload `dsh-tui-setup-win-x64.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/releases) and run it. Per-user, no administrator, fully offline, and no preinstalled Node or DSH.\n\n### Command-line installation\n\nPrerequisites: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) and\n[deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).\nThe `deepseek-official` API-key route needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. On DSH\n0.2.0-rc.1+, the standard profile can instead use `/auth login deepseek-account`\nand select the separate account route through `/model`. Other supported\naccounts can sign in through `/provider` or `/auth` after startup.\n\nThe primary compatibility target is DSH `0.2.2-rc.1`. This adapter supports its\nShell API, V4 session messages, declarative presets, and profile-backed settings;\nolder supported hosts retain their compatibility paths. See [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md).\n\nOn DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later, `/settings` also selects DeepSeek Search / Fetch APIs and edits their\nendpoint and result limits, supporting custom Loader entry IDs and a masked API\nkey input saved through DSH's credential store. Official Flash model labels show the `1017` release\nmarker while retaining the `deepseek-flash` model ID.\n\n`/settings` groups its sections into pages: the TUI's own settings sit under\n**General**, and plugins that declare a page get their own tab (`Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, or a click on the strip in fullscreen, switches pages; the strip is hidden when only one page exists).\n\nOn DSH 0.1.7, `/settings` uses the TUI's actual Loader entry ID, including custom\nIDs. It requires matching profile dependencies with `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`\n3.18.3 or newer; an incompatible schema stops TUI startup with repair guidance\ninstead of showing an uneditable settings page. Older hosts keep their legacy settings scope.\n\nThe `dsh-tui` section of `/settings` is saved in `~/.dsh-tui/settings.json`, shared by\nevery kernel; the first launch imports it once from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (and an older host's `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`)\n(see [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md#tui-configuration)).\n\n```sh\n# Install the CLI and this plugin globally (ships the dsh-tui command)\nnpm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui\n\n# Start (first run auto-initializes the profile; needs pnpm)\ndsh-tui\n# Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI.\ndst\n```\n\nManual alternative: `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`.\nThe repo's `sh install.sh` runs that step and checks the required commands.\nAfterwards `dsh-tui` and `dsh --profile dsh-tui` are equivalent.\n\n> **New-user note**: pnpm ≥11 blocks dependencies with install scripts by\n> default and reports `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. Updates skip foreign-platform\n> natives — the `@img/sharp-*` packages and the Claude SDK's per-platform\n> bundles — so only this machine's binaries are fetched. `/update` and\n> `dsh-tui update` write both settings automatically. An update never installs\n> the Claude SDK on its own: it enters a profile only when you pick that\n> backend in the kernel picker, which then installs the pinned SDK for the\n> running platform. No manual step needed. Details:\n> [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#pnpm-install-script-blocks-and-foreign-platform-natives).\n\nAfter startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never\nblocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade of the whole set\n— TUI, dsh engine and global launcher. It restarts automatically and resumes\nthe current session, and refuses instead of leaving an incompatible or\nunbootable TUI/engine combination. Launcher alignment is normally best effort,\nbut a failure after the engine advances blocks the restart and prints a repair\ncommand. If the registry has a newer dsh release outside the TUI's\nvalidated line, it says so and waits for a TUI update rather than installing an\nunvalidated engine. Launcher alignment only touches proven global installs;\nlocal npm/npx packages, ambiguous aliases and multi-member pnpm groups stay\nunchanged. See\n[Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle,\nsource builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former\n`dsh-cc-tui` package.\n\n### CLI\n\nAutomation: `dst -p \"task\"`, `dst run --json`, `dst session list --json`.\nThe independent engine does not load the TUI or inherit its profile/preferences;\nit uses official DSH headless/services (validated on 0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.3, 0.2.1-rc.4 and 0.2.1-rc.5).\n`dst cli --help` lists its commands; `dst dsh <argv...>` forwards native DSH.\nSee [Automation CLI](docs/cli.en.md) for protocol, limits, resume restrictions,\nand Node/Python/PowerShell integration examples.\n\n| Command | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program |\n| `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · align the TUI, dsh engine and global launcher as one set · pre-flight environment checks |\n| `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile |\n| `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install |\n\nLeading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch <path>` are forwarded\nunchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use\n`dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal\nprompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH\ndirectly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first\n`--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal\nprompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay\nand sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session.\nSafe mode: [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md).\n\n### Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)\n\nBring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`:\n\n```sh\ndsh-tui migrate                # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing)\ndsh-tui migrate claude-code    # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build)\ndsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run  # preview what would land, write nothing\n```\n\n- **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable).\n- **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates.\n- **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up.\nIn-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it.\nIn-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate <agent> [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow.\nCLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import.\nFull guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md).\n\n- More agents (pi, opencode, …) extend the adapter registry as adapters land; grok-build reads `GROK_HOME` when set.\n\n**VS Code**: use the integrated terminal or the `dsh-tui-vscode` extension. See [VS Code guide](docs/vscode.en.md). **Herdr**: run `dsh-tui` in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane; `idle` / `working` / `blocked` are reported through its local integration API. **Any terminal**: dsh-tui reports `idle` / `working` / `blocked` / `done` / `error` over the pty with [OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agentic inboxes that implement it can show what the session is doing; terminals that do not implement it ignore the sequence. Set `DSH_TUI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn it off.\n\nBare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this\nlaunch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no\nlast session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one\nthat actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming\na backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's\nsource), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start,\nnever another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume <id>`\npasses that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's\n\"retry normal startup\": it retries the kernel and session recorded in\n`last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold\nstart — that retry is the last way back.\n\n### Experimental: Claude backend\n\ndsh-TUI can also run its session on Claude: the same interface, driving the\nClaude Code CLI through the Claude Agent SDK. Your project's `CLAUDE.md`,\nsettings, hooks, MCP servers and plugins load as the CLI loads them.\n\n```sh\n# once, in the dsh-tui profile directory (the SDK is an optional dependency)\ncd ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-tui && pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.287\ndsh-tui --backend claude     # or pick Claude in /kernel; that choice is remembered\n```\n\nThe easiest install: open the kernel picker (the launchpad \"Kernel\" entry or\n`/kernel`) and press Enter on the dim Claude row — the wizard locates the\nprofile directory and installs the pinned SDK for you; the command above is\nits manual equivalent.\nThe confirmation shows the exact package and version. Closing the wizard,\nincluding clicking outside it on the launchpad, cancels a pending installation.\n\n- **Sign-in**: a `/channel` relay profile, your dsh-auth `anthropic` sign-in\n  (`/login`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or cloud-provider variables, or an existing\n  `claude login`, in that order. A `claude` on `PATH` is used when present, then\n  one in the native install directory under your home (`~/.local/bin`, or\n  `%USERPROFILE%\\.local\\bin` on Windows); every candidate has to launch and\n  report a version, and the SDK's bundled binary is used only when none does.\n- **Works**: streaming, tool cards, approvals and questions, `/model`,\n  `/effort`, Claude's permission modes (`/permission`, `Shift+Tab`),\n  `/compact`, `/context`, `/mcp`, `/resume`, `/fork`, double-`Esc` rewind,\n  subagents, background jobs, images, `/btw`, and the USD cost Claude reports.\n- **Not available**: DSH-only commands such as `/tree`, `/preset`,\n  `/provider`, `/workspace`, `/agentview` and `/bg`. One process runs one\n  backend; `/kernel` switches by restarting into a new session.\n- **Startup**: the screen appears before the session opens, with only a light\n  profile composed (this package plus the profile's third-party plugins); see\n  [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md#known-limitations). The DSH kernel\n  starts from the same entry and loads DSH in the same process behind its first\n  screen; `DSH_TUI_HOST_ENTRY=0` restores the old launch path for every kernel.\n\nDetails and known limitations: [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md).\n\n### Experimental: native Codex backend\n\nRun your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration,\nlogin, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads:\n\n```sh\nnpm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1\ndsh-tui --backend codex\ndsh-tui --backend codex --resume <thread-id>\n```\n\nProtocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show\ndrift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend.\n`codex resume <id>` can open the same thread after the other writer exits.\nThis is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH.\nWith native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the\nofficial background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed\nsubscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes.\n\nStreaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and\neffort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP\nshare the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex\ncontinues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and\ndismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying\npermission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex\nsettings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers\nChatGPT OAuth, a device code or an API key (the last writes to Codex’s own\ncredential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed\nsubscription tokens are only injected on first-party routes. dsh-TUI does\nnot write `~/.codex/config.toml` or log out your native Codex account. A\nprovider `env_key` from your own config (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) that the\nshell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref\nis stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so\nkeep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed.       "content": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * dsh-tui — 双态启动器（delegating launcher，0.9.3）。\n *\n * 同一个文件按“自己住在哪”决定扮演的角色：\n *\n *   全局安装副本（npm i -g 得到的 `dsh-tui` 命令）→ 瘦壳：\n *     1. 找到 $DSH_HOME/profiles/dsh-tui 里的同包 bin；\n *     2. 可读 → 原样转发 argv 委托它执行（完整逻辑永远来自 profile 副本，\n *        版本随 /update 一起前进，启动器滞后问题从结构上消失）；\n *     3. 不可读（首次运行）→ 探测 dsh/pnpm 后自举\n *        `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add <本包>@<本包版本>`，成功后委托。\n *\n *   profile 内副本（被委托执行，或 junction/源码目录里直接运行）→ 完整\n *   启动逻辑（与 0.8.6 及之前一致）：\n *     dsh 预检 / profile 版本核对 / --resume 与工作区目标拦截 /\n *     `dsh --profile dsh-tui` 启动与退出码透传。\n *\n * 自举角色判定用 realpath：Windows Junction 轨（profile 指回仓库）与\n * `pnpm run dev` 源码运行都会折叠成同一物理目录 → 走完整逻辑，不会\n * 自己委托自己形成循环。\n *\n * 本文件必须保持零 lib/ 依赖：/update 的启动器迁移只覆写这一个文件\n * （外加 package.json 的版本号），旧全局安装里不存在新 lib 助手时同样\n * 可用。shellQuote 等小工具在此内联。\n *\n * 面向用户的消息走 MSG 双语表：与 TUI 的语言契约一致——\n * `DSH_TUI_LANG` 显式指定时从其值，否则默认中文（同 src/i18n.ts 的缺省）。\n */\nimport { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'\nimport { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, realpathSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { homedir } from 'node:os'\nimport { dirname, isAbsolute, join, resolve } from 'node:path'\nimport { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'\n\n// 进程名（issue #1831）：Linux 的 ps/top/桌面进程监视器显示的是主线程名\n// （/proc/<pid>/stat 的 comm 字段），Node 启动时把它设成 \"MainThread\"，启动器\n// 这两层进程同样认不出来。写 /proc/self/comm 只改线程名、不动 argv——cmdline\n// 保留入口路径，工具与回归（verify-installed-startup）靠它识别进程；只读 /proc\n// 的环境里静默保持原名。本文件必须零 lib/ 依赖，所以这十行内联，语义与\n// src/utils/processName.ts 一致（两边改动同步）。不带换行：内核原样存字节，\n// comm 里混入换行会让 ps 显示成 dsh-tui?
